**RE: Member Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Skyler Foster
*   **Member ID:** W718345521
*   **Plan:** Tufts Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Rhode Island
*   **Reference Number:** POC-BDD7B46260-11524
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (Lumbar Microdiscectomy)
*   **Procedure Code:** CPT 63030
*   **Provider:** Duval, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for my lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030), which is scheduled to be performed by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval. Tufts Health Plan denied this request on August 22, 2026, stating that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." 

This determination is contradicted by my actual clinical records and diagnostic imaging. The medical necessity of this procedure is fully supported under the governing medical policy utilized by Tufts Health Plan, **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery** (Guideline Number: Evolent_CG_3041766). 

Below, I have mapped my clinical documentation directly to the specific medical-necessity criteria required under the policy.

### 1. Address of Denial Reason: Correlation of Imaging Findings
The denial stated that my imaging did not support medical necessity. However, my diagnostic imaging and physical clinical symptoms correlate perfectly.

Under the policy's **"Lumbar Discectomy/Microdiscectomy"** section, surgery is indicated when there are:
> "Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual’s symptoms/signs"

*   **My Diagnostic Evidence:** A lumbar spine MRI performed on **June 15, 2026**, reveals a **clear L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**.
*   **Clinical Correlation:** This herniation and nerve root compression correlate precisely with my clinical signs and symptoms. I suffer from severe radicular pain radiating down into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected right side, and a right-sided neurologic deficit corresponding directly to the compressed L5 nerve root level. 

The severe nerve compression shown on my MRI is the direct structural cause of my radicular symptoms. The imaging findings unequivocally support the medical necessity of CPT 63030.

### 2. Surgical Indications & Symptom Severity
The policy requires:
> "Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities"

*   **My Clinical Presentation:** I have suffered from 18 months of progressive, debilitating lower back pain that is completely unrelieved by rest. This is accompanied by severe radicular pain in my right calf. 
*   **Functional Impairment:** My condition significantly hinders my daily activities; I am currently unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. My physical examination by Dr. Duval confirmed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a corresponding neurologic deficit.

### 3. Failure of Multimodal Conservative Treatment
The policy requires:
> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ■ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR ■ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment..."

The policy defines **"*CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT"** as follows:
> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region. 
> ● Active Modalities: ○ Physical therapy...
> ● Inactive Modalities: ○ Medications (e.g., NSAIDs, steroids, analgesics) ○ Injections (e.g., epidural steroid injection, selective nerve root block)"

My medical history documents a comprehensive and failed course of conservative therapy within the last six months, meeting both the active and inactive modality criteria:
*   **Active Modality (Physical Therapy):** I completed **10 weeks of supervised physical therapy** focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility from **May 11, 2026, to July 20, 2026**. I attended and completed **20 visits**, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This far exceeds the plan's 6-week active treatment guideline.
*   **Inactive Modality (Medications):** I have been taking NSAIDs for **8 months** to manage my pain, with inadequate relief.
*   **Inactive Modality (Injections):** I underwent a **corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026**, which yielded only 4 weeks of partial pain relief before my severe symptoms returned.
*   **Documentation of Failure:** Despite undergoing these extensive multimodal conservative treatments, my pain has progressively worsened and continues to severely limit my basic mobility and function (standing for less than 10 minutes). I have experienced a complete "lack of meaningful improvement" and "progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment."

### Clinical Background & Safety Factors
Furthermore, I have no active infections, no untreated substance use disorders, am a non-smoker, and have a BMI of 29. I am an excellent candidate for this decompressive procedure, and there are no contraindications to surgery.

### Conclusion
I have completed and failed more than 10 weeks of conservative, multimodal therapy within the last six months. My lumbar MRI from June 15, 2026, shows an objective L4-L5 disc extrusion compressing the L5 nerve root, which correlates exactly with my right-sided radicular calf pain and clinical neurological deficits. 

My case meets every medical necessity requirement outlined under **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766**. I request that Tufts Health Plan immediately overturn this denial and authorize the requested lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your timely response.

Sincerely,

Skyler Foster
